Ice is made of water.
More precisely:
Ice is the solid form of water (H₂O).
It consists of the same molecules as liquid water and water vapor — two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom — but in ice, these H₂O molecules are arranged in a very organized, repeating hexagonal crystal lattice structure.
That's why ice:

Is less dense than liquid water (which is very unusual for solids)
Floats on water
Has that beautiful hexagonal symmetry you see in snowflakes

Quick summary:





























StateNameMolecular arrangementDensitySolidIceHighly organized crystal lattice~0.917 g/cm³LiquidWaterSomewhat organized, can move freely1.00 g/cm³GasWater vaporCompletely random, far apartVery low
So when someone asks "What is ice made of?" the shortest true answer is:
Ice is made of frozen water. 😄

result.text:
World War II ended in 1945.

The war in Europe ended on May 8, 1945 (Victory in Europe Day / VE Day)
The war officially ended worldwide on September 2, 1945 (when Japan formally surrendered aboard the USS Missouri, celebrated as Victory over Japan Day / VJ Day)

So while different dates are sometimes referenced depending on the theater of war, the universally accepted year WWII ended is 1945.

The largest mammal on Earth — and indeed the largest animal that has ever existed — is the blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus).
These magnificent marine giants can reach lengths of up to 30 meters (about 100 feet), with the longest reliably recorded specimen measuring around 33 meters. The heaviest verified specimen weighed 190 tonnes (about 418,000 pounds), though some estimates suggest exceptional individuals could have approached or exceeded 200 tonnes.
Here are some stunning views of these incredible creatures in their natural ocean habitat:
dreamstime.comoceanlight.com

To give you a sense of just how massive they are, here's a helpful size comparison showing a blue whale alongside humans, an elephant, and other large animals:
treehugger.com11 Facts About Blue Whales, the Largest Animal on Earth
For context:

A blue whale's heart alone can weigh as much as a small car (~180 kg).
Its tongue can weigh as much as an elephant.
A newborn blue whale calf is already about 7–8 meters long and weighs around 3 tonnes — roughly the size of a large SUV!

By comparison, the largest land mammal is the African bush elephant, which tops out at around 6–7 tonnes — impressive, but only a fraction of the blue whale's size. The ocean's buoyancy allows these colossal mammals to grow to sizes impossible for land animals.
Blue whales are currently endangered, but they remain the undisputed heavyweight champions of the animal kingdom! 🐋
